message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – A Quick Reference Guide** | Topic | Key Points | Where to Find More Info | |-------|------------|------------------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits vary by road type (e.g., 55 mph on rural interstates, 45 mph on urban interstates).
• “No‑limit” highways (e.g., I‑10, I‑35) have no posted maximum, but drivers must still obey “reasonable and prudent” speed. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Seat Belt & Child Restraint** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster. | Texas Transportation Code §545.002 | | **DUI / Alcohol** | • Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher is illegal.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21.
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | Texas Transportation Code §§545.021–545.023 | | **Texting & Phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is prohibited.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | Texas Transportation Code §545.025 | | **Headlights & Signal Use** | • Headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise and during inclement weather.
• Turn signals must be used at least 100 ft before turning. | Texas Transportation Code §545.030 | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • Stop signs, yield signs, and traffic lights are mandatory.
• Pedestrians have priority at crosswalks. | Texas Transportation Code §545.040 | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking in front of driveways, fire hydrants, or within 20 ft of a stop sign.
• Parking in handicap spaces requires a valid permit. | Texas Transportation Code §545.050 | | **School Bus Rules** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus is loading/unloading children. | Texas Transportation Code §545.060 | | **Lane Discipline** | • Drivers must stay in their lane unless changing lanes or turning. | Texas Transportation Code §545.070 | | **Vehicle Inspection & Registration** | • Annual vehicle inspection required for most vehicles.
• Registration renewal is due annually. | Texas Transportation Code §545.080 | | **Toll Roads & Bridges** | • Toll charges apply on certain interstates (e.g., I‑35W). | TxDOT Toll Operations | | **Emergency Vehicle Access** | • Drivers must pull over to the right and stop when an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches. | Texas Transportation Code §545.090 | --- ### How to Stay Updated 1. **Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT)** – Official website: [https://www.txdot.gov](https://www.txdot.gov) *Provides current statutes, rule changes, and driver education resources.* 2. **Texas Transportation Code** – Accessible online via the Texas Legislature’s website: [https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/](https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/) *Full legal text of all traffic laws.* 3. **Texas Driver Handbook** – Available in PDF form on TxDOT’s site. *Summarizes rules for new drivers and includes practice tests.* 4. **Local County Courts** – For specific enforcement actions or penalties. *County court websites often list local ordinances that supplement state law.* --- ### Quick Tips for Safe Driving in Texas - **Always keep your seat belt fastened** – it’s a simple habit that saves lives. - **Avoid distractions** – put your phone away or use hands‑free if you must talk. - **Observe speed limits** – they’re designed for safety, not convenience. - **Check for local ordinances** – some cities have stricter rules (e.g., lower speed limits, additional signage). - **Stay alert for school buses** – they have special stopping requirements. Feel free to let me know if you need deeper details on any specific area (e.g., DUI penalties, toll rates, or how to register a vehicle).
